newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi prince adds Apple stake to portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Saudi prince adds Apple stake to portfolio.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's billionaire Prince al-Waleed bin Talal said Wednesday that he has taken a 5 percent stake in Apple Computer Inc., the latest in a string of high-profile international acquisitions.

The prince said he bought the Apple shares on the open market in recent weeks for a total of $115 million, a move similar to his purchase of about 5 percent of Trans World Airlines Inc., which he announced on March 19.

"I have been following the technology industry closely for quite some time, and Apple in particular for a number of months," Prince al-Waleed said in a statement. "I believe there is serious potential for Apple to provide large returns to its stockholders once again, as it did in the past."

Referring to reports that an investor group led by Oracle Corp. Chief Executive Larry Ellison was interested in making a bid for a controlling interest in the struggling computer maker, the prince said he "will monitor events closely" to see what steps are taken by Ellison, Apple's management, or by others, to improve returns to Apple stockholders.

Also in March, the billionaire nephew of King Fahd of Saudi Arabia announced he was buying a 5 percent stake in Norwegian Cruise Lines for $20 million and said he was building a $500 million complex in Riyadh, his hometown and the Saudi capital, to house a Four Seasons Hotel, the largest commercial building in the region.

Though not huge compared with the prince's other holdings, the new investments are part of a new business trend of diversifying his investments away from real estate and entertainment, financial sources close to the prince said.
"He has been looking into these companies for some time now. He is also considering other similar international acquisitions," one said, but refused to elaborate.
The prince told Reuters last month: "I have a big portfolio and this is part of diversification."
Financial analysts said the new investments were part of the prince's policy of buying stakes in ailing companies and trying to put them back on their feet.
The trend might also include bankrupt Dutch plane maker Fokker, for which the prince has emerged as a possible saviour.
Prince al-Waleed -- who turned 40 on March 7 -- is a grandson of Saudi Arabia's founder, Ibn Saud.
People who know him say he started with a relatively small amount of money from his father and is now one of the wealthiest and most powerful business moguls in the kingdom.

Surrounded by a close circle of advisers, he controls a portfolio that includes shares in U.S. banking giant Citicorp., retailer Saks Fifth Avenue and the Plaza Hotel, the Euro Disney theme park near Paris and Canary Wharf in London's Docklands.

He also has stakes in former Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's television and advertising business Mediaset and huge property holdings that include the Fairmont and Four Seasons hotel chains.
Earlier this year he bought Paris' luxury George V hotel.
Last year he signed a deal with popstar Michael Jackson to cooperate on concerts, films, television, fun parks and hotels.
